drafts.title: Hypothetical RAG Sanity Check: Evaluating Retrieval Impact
drafts.body: I'm outlining a hypothetical experiment to sanity-check a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) setup. The core idea is to compare model responses to the same set of questions under two conditions: with retrieval enabled and with retrieval disabled. This comparison aims to isolate the impact of the retrieved context on the generated output, using a local corpus of 30 documents. We'll include questions designed to be unanswerable from the provided documents to observe how the system behaves when information is absent. It's crucial to remember this is a purely hypothetical scenario; no actual performance data or accuracy results are being presented. The objective is to discuss the design considerations for such an evaluation and how to interpret the hypothetical outputs. What factors should be prioritized when setting up this kind of test?

drafts.title: Designing a Hypothetical RAG Evaluation: Retrieval On vs. Off
drafts.body: This post proposes a hypothetical framework for evaluating a RAG system's retrieval component. The experiment involves using 30 local documents as the knowledge base. The central methodology is to pose a set of questions twice: once with the RAG retrieval mechanism active and once with it bypassed. This allows for a direct, albeit hypothetical, comparison of responses. We are specifically including questions that have no corresponding answer within the 30 documents to test the system's handling of information gaps. It's important to stress that this is a theoretical exercise, and no actual measured results or accuracy figures are available. The goal is to stimulate discussion on how to best design and interpret such a hypothetical evaluation, particularly concerning the differences observed between retrieval-on and retrieval-off outputs.

drafts.title: Hypothetical RAG Sanity Check: Evaluating Retrieval Effectiveness with Unanswerable Questions
drafts.body: I'm exploring a hypothetical RAG sanity check focused on retrieval effectiveness. The proposed setup uses a collection of 30 local documents. The core of the evaluation involves comparing model responses to the same questions, first with retrieval enabled, and then with retrieval disabled. This approach aims to highlight how the retrieved context influences the output, or if the model relies solely on its internal knowledge. A key element of this hypothetical experiment is the inclusion of questions for which no answer can be found within the 30 documents. This is intended to probe the system's behavior in information-scarce scenarios. Please note that this remains a theoretical exercise, and no actual accuracy metrics or performance results are available. The main question is: what are the critical considerations for designing such a hypothetical evaluation and interpreting the output differences?
drafts.plan: Rephrase the title to emphasize the specific evaluation aspect. Ensure the body clearly states the hypothetical nature upfront. Structure the post to present the setup, the purpose, the limitations, and the discussion prompt concisely.
